e.title: 车险欺诈评分：把测试集 PR-AUC 1.00 当作 bug 报告，并写一条「模型不许太好」的集成测试
e.title_en: Auto claim fraud scoring: treating a test-set PR-AUC of 1.00 as a bug report, and writing an integration test that the model must not get too good
e.title_hk: 車險欺詐評分：把測試集 PR-AUC 1.00 當作 bug 報告，並寫一條「模型不許太好」的集成測試
e.summary: 一个端到端的车险理赔欺诈评分系统：dbt 特征层含 44 项数据质量测试、兼顾类别不平衡的 XGBoost 配 SHAP 可解释性、FastAPI 评分服务与 Streamlit 复核台；它把开发中出现的测试集 PR-AUC 1.00 当作数据泄漏线索而非成绩，定位到两个「留一法」欺诈率编码特征并移除，再补一条集成测试断言 PR-AUC 必须低于 0.95，防止它悄悄回来
e.summary_hk: 一個端到端的車險理賠欺詐評分系統：dbt 特徵層含 44 項資料質量測試、兼顧類別不平衡的 XGBoost 配 SHAP 可解釋性、FastAPI 評分服務與 Streamlit 複核台；它把開發中出現的測試集 PR-AUC 1.00 當作資料洩漏線索而非成績，定位到兩個「留一法」欺詐率編碼特徵並移除，再補一條集成測試斷言 PR-AUC 必須低於 0.95，防止它悄悄回來
e.summary_en: An end-to-end auto claim fraud risk scoring system: a dbt feature layer with 44 data-quality tests, a class-imbalance-aware XGBoost model with SHAP explainability, a FastAPI scoring service and a Streamlit reviewer dashboard; it treats a test-set PR-AUC of 1.00 encountered during development as a leakage clue rather than a result, traces it to two leave-one-out fraud-rate encodings, removes them, and adds an integration test asserting PR-AUC must stay below 0.95 so the leak cannot silently return
e.body:
**insurance-fraud-risk-scoring** 是一个**端到端的车险理赔欺诈评分系统**（仓库 `cher-ry2003/insurance-fraud-risk-scoring`），**实测 MIT 许可（根目录实测含 `LICENSE`）、★0、fork 0、主语言 Python、仓库体量 257 KB、创建与最后推送均为 2026-09-07**（**均 GitHub API 实测值，在解冻窗口内**）；**无 topics**；**README 实测 16,738 字节**。本条目属于本轮主题**「不肯只给一个数」**中的**第一种，也是把这条原则推到最极端的一种：它主动把一个「完美成绩」定性为缺陷**。

可核实信息（**均 README 与仓库根目录实测**）：**根目录实测 17 项**，含 **`LICENSE`、`.env.example`、`.github`、`.streamlit`、`api/`、`dashboard/`、`data/`、`dbt/`、`docs/`、`fraud_risk/`、`models/`、`notebooks/`、`pyproject.toml`、`scripts/`、`tests/`**。**其自我定位逐字，是本条目最重要的一段**：**「This is a portfolio project built to demonstrate how I’d approach a fraud scoring problem on a real insurance/health claims team — **the emphasis is on the engineering and judgment calls around the model (data quality, leakage, imbalance, explainability, honest limitations), not on squeezing out the last percentage point of a leaderboard metric**.」**。

对 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 「测试集 PR-AUC 1.00 不是一个值得骄傲的结果，而是一份 bug 报告」是本条目最有价值的一句话，也是本会话见到对**完美指标**最正确的处理**——**逐字为**：**「The first end-to-end run of this pipeline reported **PR-AUC = 1.00** — a perfect fraud classifier. **That is never a result to report proudly; it’s a signal something is wrong.**」**，**并在摘要处逐字重述**：**「That’s not a result to be proud of — **it’s a bug report**.」**（**可与第 331 轮 [[aida-tix-anomaly-detection]] 的「AUC 0.46 读作失败、读对了才是重点」并读——**两条恰好从**过高**与**过低**两端处理同一个问题：**指标本身不构成结论****）。**② ⭐⭐⭐ **其四步排查过程逐字实测，是一份可照搬的泄漏排查清单**：**① 先列出可疑特征**——`vehicle_segment_flagged_ratio_loo` 与 `incident_city_flagged_ratio_loo` 是**留一法（leave-one-out）欺诈率编码**，**逐字说明「a claim’s own label never enters its own group statistic, which is the **textbook way to avoid target leakage from mean encoding**」**（**即它们按教科书做法本应是安全的**）；**② 只删这两个特征**，**测试 PR-AUC 从 1.00 掉到 0.57**——**既确认了病因，也排除了训练循环本身有 bug**；**③ 定位根因**——⭐⭐⭐ **逐字为**：**「in this specific synthetic dataset, fraud probability appears to have been **baked into vehicle make/model and incident-city groupings by the data generator itself**. **A textbook leakage-safe encoding still becomes a near-alias for the label when the grouping variable *is* the generative rule** — a failure mode that has nothing to do with the encoding technique being unsound and everything to do with this dataset’s synthetic origin.」**——**即「在这份特定的合成数据集里，欺诈概率似乎是**由数据生成器本身烘焙进车辆品牌／车型与出险城市分组里的**；**当**分组变量本身就等于生成规则**时，一个教科书式的防泄漏编码**仍会变成标签的近似别名****」；**④ 处置**：**两个特征从建模特征集中移除**，**而 dbt 仍计算底层的暴露／异常列**（`vehicle_segment_claim_count`、`_avg_claim_loo`、`_stddev_claim_loo`——**逐字理由是「since those aren’t the label-adjacent ones」**）。⭐⭐⭐ **本词条认为第 ③ 步的洞察值得单独记住**：**「防泄漏技术」防的是**编码方式**带来的泄漏，防不住**数据生成过程本身把标签写进了特征**——**后者不是技巧问题，而是合成数据的性质问题**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**该根因分析已获独立验证**——**本次未读其 `fraud_risk/features.py`，亦未复现**）。**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **它把这次教训固化成了两条测试，其中一条断言「模型不许太好」**——**逐字为**：**「A regression test (`tests/test_features.py::test_leaky_features_stay_excluded`) and an integration test (`tests/test_train.py`, **asserting PR-AUC stays under 0.95**) guard against this silently coming back.」**⭐⭐⭐ **「断言 PR-AUC 低于 0.95」是一条**反向断言**：**通常的模型测试断言「不低于某个下限」，而这条断言**上限****——**它把**「这次泄漏的指纹」编码成了测试****；**对做模型验证的学生，这是一个**把一次性人工发现变成永久防线**的具体做法**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**这两条测试确实存在或能通过**——**本次未运行 pytest，未读 `tests/`**）。**④ ⭐⭐⭐ **第二处处理更精妙：一个「不可信的特征」被**故意保留**，只为了让解释层把它暴露出来**——**逐字为**：**「`insured_hobbies` values **`chess` (82.6% fraud)** and **`cross-fit` (74.3% fraud)** are wildly out of line with every other hobby and the **24.7% base rate** — see the SHAP plot below, where they show up as the **#2 and #3 most important features**. **There’s no plausible real-world mechanism where hobby predicts insurance fraud this strongly; this reads as another artifact of the synthetic generation process.** Unlike the leaky loo-features, this one was **kept** in the model **on purpose** (`FEATURE_CAVEATS` in `fraud_risk/features.py`) **so SHAP surfaces it** — and **the API/dashboard both emit an explicit warning whenever it appears in a claim’s top contributing features, rather than a reviewer trusting a score without knowing part of it rests on a feature this project doesn’t itself trust**.」**⭐⭐⭐ **对做可解释 AI 的学生，这是本会话见到对**已知不可信特征**最成熟的处理**：**既不隐藏也不静默删除，而是保留它、让解释层曝露它、并在它起作用时主动声明****（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**该警告在实际响应中确实触发**——**本次未调用其 API**）。**⑤ ⭐⭐ **其余工程面逐字实测且都属可核实的交代**：**dbt 特征层含 **44 项数据测试**（`not_null`／`accepted_values`／`relationships`／自定义 range 与 singular），**其中一项**抓到了源数据中的真实异常****；**数据仓**本地用 DuckDB（零配置）、生产用 Snowflake，**同一份 dbt 项目只切换 target****；**类别不平衡的处理**经论证与比较**（class weighting 与 SMOTE 两法）；**训练脚本含 logreg 基线 + XGBoost**；**可解释性用 SHAP TreeExplainer**；**评分 API 逐字返回「**probability + SHAP explanation + caveats**」**——⭐ **即**警示本身是响应契约的一部分****；**`notebooks/` 被逐字标注为「exploration only」**；**数据目录内含 `data/README.md`（source & limitations）**；**模型目录含训练产物 + `metrics.json` + `feature_spec.json`**。**⑥ ⭐⭐ **数据说明与追问入口都写在明面上**：**数据集为 1,000 行**合成**车险理赔数据（原出自 IBM Watson 样本）**；**完整写法与「实际数字」指向 `fraud_risk/features.py` 的 `EXCLUDED_FEATURES` 与 `notebooks/01_eda.ipynb`**——⭐⭐ **即它把**争议细节**留在了**可直接打开的文件**里，而不只是留在叙述中**。**⑦ ⭐ 可与本站欺诈与可解释性条目并读**：[[explainable-ai-fraud]]、[[ifraudsimulator]]、[[networkfraud]]、[[insurance-conformal-fraud]]、[[fraud-detection]]、[[claims-fraud-guardian]]、[[aida-tix-anomaly-detection]]、[[claim-fraud-dataset-generator]]、[[aws-gnn-fraud-detection]]、[[shap-relativities]]。

⚠️ **如实标注**：**①** 本次核实的是**仓库元数据、仓库根目录清单（17 项，含 `LICENSE`）与 README（16,738 字节）全文的定位段、泄漏排查四步、两条防护测试、`insured_hobbies` 处置、架构图、技术栈、仓库结构与数据集段**，⭐⭐ **但**未克隆、未安装、未运行训练或评分、未执行 `pytest` 或任何 dbt 测试、未调用其 FastAPI 服务或 Streamlit 仪表板、未读 `fraud_risk/`／`api/`／`dashboard/`／`dbt/` 下任何源码、未读 `notebooks/01_eda.ipynb`、未读 `data/README.md` 与 `models/` 下的产物****，因此**不能转述其 dbt 模型定义、特征工程实现、模型超参数、SHAP 输出或任何数值**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **未核实**「PR-AUC 曾达 1.00、删除两个特征后降至 0.57」这一排查过程的真实性**——**本次未运行其流水线、未复现该数字**；**本词条只记录其**自述的排查经过与方法论**，**不主张**该过程确如所述**；**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **未核实**那两条防护测试（`test_leaky_features_stay_excluded` 与断言 PR-AUC 低于 0.95 的集成测试）确实存在且能通过**——**本次完全未运行 pytest、未读 `tests/`**；**这是本条目最需要后续核实的一处**；**④ ⭐⭐⭐ **未核实** `insured_hobbies` 中 `chess` 82.6%／`cross-fit` 74.3%／基础率 24.7% 这几个数值**，**亦未核实**「API 与仪表板在该特征进入前几位贡献时确实发出警告」**——**本次未调用其服务**；**⑤ ⭐⭐ **未核实**其 44 项 dbt 测试中「一项抓到源数据真实异常」的具体所指**；**⑥ ⭐⭐ **未核实**其根因判断（「欺诈概率被数据生成器烘焙进车辆与城市分组」）**——**该判断基于本仓库作者对一份第三方合成数据的观察**，**本词条**不主张**其适用于其他数据集，**亦不主张**其已获原数据集作者确认**；**⑦ ⭐ **未核实**其「同一份 dbt 项目在 DuckDB 与 Snowflake 间切换」的可行性**（**未运行**）；**⑧ ⭐ ⚠️ **所选数据集为**合成的 1,000 行样本****，**且其自述 `insured_hobbies` 等字段与真实世界机制不符**；**本词条据此**不主张**其模型、指标或结论可外推到任何真实理赔组合**；**⑨ ⭐ ⚠️ 欺诈评分用于**对个人作出不利判断**的场景**——**在多数辖区涉及程序与合规要求**；**本词条**不主张**该系统可用于任何真实的理赔调查、拒赔或对个人的不利行动**；**⑩ ⭐ **README 未讨论公平性／受保护类别影响**（**与同轮 [[guidewire-claim-intelligence]] 明确把公平性审计列为应增加的一等评估标准形成对照**）——**本词条仅记录这一差异，不作价值判断**；**⑪ ⭐ ★0、fork 0、创建与推送同日**，**关注度极低**，**不主张其成熟度、正确性或已被采用**；**⑫ ⭐ 无 topics**；**⑬ 是否有中文材料本次未核实**（**README 实测为英文**）。**核实说明**：`https://api.github.com/repos/cher-ry2003/insurance-fraud-risk-scoring`、`/readme` 与 `/contents/` 于 2026-09-11 经 GitHub API 实测读取（README 16,738 字节经 `raw.githubusercontent.com` 实测逐字核对）；**未克隆、未安装、未运行、未读源码与 notebooks**。

**insurance-fraud-risk-scoring** 是一個**端到端的車險理賠欺詐評分系統**（倉庫 `cher-ry2003/insurance-fraud-risk-scoring`），**實測 MIT 許可（根目錄實測含 `LICENSE`）、★0、fork 0、主語言 Python、體量 257 KB、創建與最後推送均為 2026-09-07**（**在解凍窗口內**）；**無 topics**；**README 實測 16,738 位元組**。本條目屬本輪主題**「不肯只給一個數」**中的**第一種，也是把這條原則推到最極端的一種：它主動把一個「完美成績」定性為缺陷**。

可核實資訊（**均 README 與倉庫根目錄實測**）：**根目錄實測 17 項**，含 **`LICENSE`、`.env.example`、`.github`、`.streamlit`、`api/`、`dashboard/`、`data/`、`dbt/`、`docs/`、`fraud_risk/`、`models/`、`notebooks/`、`scripts/`、`tests/`**。**其自我定位逐字**：**「This is a portfolio project built to demonstrate how I’d approach a fraud scoring problem on a real insurance/health claims team — **the emphasis is on the engineering and judgment calls around the model (data quality, leakage, imbalance, explainability, honest limitations), not on squeezing out the last percentage point of a leaderboard metric**.」**。

對 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 「測試集 PR-AUC 1.00 不是值得驕傲的結果，而是一份 bug 報告」是最有價值的一句**——**逐字「The first end-to-end run of this pipeline reported **PR-AUC = 1.00** — a perfect fraud classifier. **That is never a result to report proudly; it’s a signal something is wrong.**」**，**並逐字重述「That’s not a result to be proud of — **it’s a bug report**.」**（可與第 331 輪 [[aida-tix-anomaly-detection]] 的「AUC 0.46 讀作失敗、讀對了才是重點」並讀——**兩條恰好從**過高**與**過低**兩端處理同一問題：**指標本身不構成結論****）。**② ⭐⭐⭐ **四步排查逐字，是一份可照搬的洩漏排查清單**：① 列出可疑特徵——`vehicle_segment_flagged_ratio_loo` 與 `incident_city_flagged_ratio_loo` 是**留一法欺詐率編碼**，**逐字含「a claim’s own label never enters its own group statistic, which is the **textbook way to avoid target leakage from mean encoding**」**；② 只刪這兩個特徵後**測試 PR-AUC 從 1.00 掉到 0.57**，**既確認病因也排除了訓練循環本身有 bug**；③ 定位根因——⭐⭐⭐ **逐字「A textbook leakage-safe encoding still becomes a near-alias for the label when the grouping variable *is* the generative rule** — a failure mode that has nothing to do with the encoding technique being unsound and everything to do with this dataset’s synthetic origin.」**——**即**當分組變數本身就等於生成規則**時，教科書式防洩漏編碼仍會變成標籤的近似別名**；④ 處置：兩個特徵從建模集移除，**而 dbt 仍計算底層暴露／異常列**（`vehicle_segment_claim_count`、`_avg_claim_loo`、`_stddev_claim_loo`——「since those aren’t the label-adjacent ones」）。⭐⭐⭐ **第 ③ 步的洞察值得單獨記住**：**「防洩漏技術」防的是**編碼方式**帶來的洩漏，防不住**資料生成過程本身把標籤寫進了特徵****（**⚠️ 不主張**該根因分析已獲獨立驗證**）。**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **它把教訓固化成兩條測試，其中一條斷言「模型不許太好」**——**逐字「A regression test (`tests/test_features.py::test_leaky_features_stay_excluded`) and an integration test (`tests/test_train.py`, **asserting PR-AUC stays under 0.95**) guard against this silently coming back.」**⭐⭐⭐ **「斷言 PR-AUC 低於 0.95」是一條**反向斷言****——**通常的模型測試斷言不低於某個下限，而這條斷言**上限**，把「這次洩漏的指紋」編碼成了測試**（**⚠️ 未運行 pytest、未讀 `tests/`**）。**④ ⭐⭐⭐ **第二處處理更精妙：一個「不可信的特徵」被**故意保留**，只為了讓解釋層把它暴露出來**——**逐字「`insured_hobbies` values **`chess` (82.6% fraud)** and **`cross-fit` (74.3% fraud)** are wildly out of line with every other hobby and the **24.7% base rate** … **There’s no plausible real-world mechanism where hobby predicts insurance fraud this strongly; **insurance-fraud-risk-scoring** is **an end-to-end auto claim fraud risk scoring system** (repository `cher-ry2003/insurance-fraud-risk-scoring`), with **measured MIT licence (a `LICENSE` file is present at the root), ★0, 0 forks, Python as the primary language, a 257 KB repository, created and last pushed 2026-09-07** (**all GitHub API measurements, inside the thaw window**); it has **no topics**; **the README measures 16,738 bytes**. It is the first of this round’s four takes on **refusing to give just one number**, **and the one that pushes the principle furthest: it reclassifies a perfect score as a defect**.

Verifiable details (**all measured from the README and the repository root**): **the root measurably contains 17 items**, including **`LICENSE`, `.env.example`, `.github`, `.streamlit`, `api/`, `dashboard/`, `data/`, `dbt/`, `docs/`, `fraud_risk/`, `models/`, `notebooks/`, `scripts/` and `tests/`**. **Its self-positioning, read verbatim, is the entry’s most important passage**: **"This is a portfolio project built to demonstrate how I’d approach a fraud scoring problem on a real insurance/health claims team — the emphasis is on the engineering and judgment calls around the model (data quality, leakage, imbalance, explainability, honest limitations), not on squeezing out the last percentage point of a leaderboard metric."**

For RIAA: **① ⭐⭐⭐ "A test-set PR-AUC of 1.00 is not something to be proud of — it is a bug report" is the entry’s most valuable sentence, and the most correct handling of a perfect metric this session has seen** — verbatim: **"The first end-to-end run of this pipeline reported PR-AUC = 1.00 — a perfect fraud classifier. That is never a result to report proudly; it’s a signal something is wrong."**, **restated verbatim as**: **"That’s not a result to be proud of — it’s a bug report."** (**readable with round 331’s [[aida-tix-anomaly-detection]] and its "AUC 0.46 read as failure, read correctly it’s the point" — the two handle the same problem from the too-high and too-low ends: a metric is not itself a conclusion**). **② ⭐⭐⭐ Its four-step investigation reads verbatim and is a portable leakage checklist**: **① name the suspects** — `vehicle_segment_flagged_ratio_loo` and `incident_city_flagged_ratio_loo` are **leave-one-out fraud-rate encodings**, and **"a claim’s own label never enters its own group statistic, which is the textbook way to avoid target leakage from mean encoding"** (i.e. by the book they should have been safe); **② drop only those two features**, and **test PR-AUC falls from 1.00 to 0.57** — **confirming the cause while ruling out a training-loop bug**; **③ identify the root cause** — ⭐⭐⭐ verbatim: **"in this specific synthetic dataset, fraud probability appears to have been baked into vehicle make/model and incident-city groupings by the data generator itself. A textbook leakage-safe encoding still becomes a near-alias for the label when the grouping variable *is* the generative rule — a failure mode that has nothing to do with the encoding technique being unsound and everything to do with this dataset’s synthetic origin."**; **④ disposition** — **both features removed from the modelled set**, **while dbt still computes the underlying exposure and anomaly columns** (`vehicle_segment_claim_count`, `_avg_claim_loo`, `_stddev_claim_loo` — **"since those aren’t the label-adjacent ones"**). ⭐⭐⭐ **Step ③ deserves to be remembered on its own: leakage-safe technique guards against leakage introduced by the encoding, not against a data-generating process that writes the label into a feature — the latter is not a technique problem but a property of synthetic data** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim the root-cause analysis has been independently verified — its `fraud_risk/features.py` was not read and nothing was reproduced**). **③ ⭐⭐⭐ It hardens the lesson into two tests, one of which asserts the model must not get too good** — verbatim: **"A regression test (`tests/test_features.py::test_leaky_features_stay_excluded`) and an integration test (`tests/test_train.py`, asserting PR-AUC stays under 0.95) guard against this silently coming back."** ⭐⭐⭐ **Asserting PR-AUC below 0.95 is a reverse assertion: model tests usually assert a floor, whereas this asserts a ceiling — encoding the leak’s fingerprint as a test**; **for students of model validation, a concrete way to turn a one-off human discovery into a permanent guard** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim those two tests exist or pass — pytest was not run and `tests/` was not read**). **④ ⭐⭐⭐ The second treatment is subtler still: a distrusted feature is deliberately kept so the explanation layer will surface it** — verbatim: **"`insured_hobbies` values `chess` (82.6% fraud) and `cross-fit` (74.3% fraud) are wildly out of line with every other hobby and the 24.7% base rate — see the SHAP plot below, where they show up as the #2 and #3 most important features. There’s no plausible real-world mechanism where hobby predicts insurance fraud this strongly; this reads as another artifact of the synthetic generation process. Unlike the leaky loo-features, this one was kept in the model on purpose (`FEATURE_CAVEATS` in `fraud_risk/features.py`) so SHAP surfaces it — and the API/dashboard both emit an explicit warning whenever it appears in a claim’s top contributing features, rather than a reviewer trusting a score without knowing part of it rests on a feature this project doesn’t itself trust."** ⭐⭐⭐ **The most mature handling of a known-untrustworthy feature this session has seen: neither hidden nor silently dropped, but kept so the explanation layer exposes it, with an explicit warning whenever it drives a score** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim the warning actually fires — its API was not called**). **⑤ ⭐⭐ The remaining engineering reads verbatim and is checkable**: **the dbt layer carries 44 data tests** (`not_null`, `accepted_values`, `relationships`, custom range and singular), **one of which caught a real anomaly in the source data**; **DuckDB locally and Snowflake in production, the same dbt project with only the target swapped**; **class-imbalance handling argued and compared** (class weighting versus SMOTE); **training with a logreg baseline plus XGBoost**; **SHAP TreeExplainer for explainability**; **and the scoring API returning verbatim "probability + SHAP explanation + caveats"** — ⭐ **the caveat is part of the response contract**; **`notebooks/` is labelled verbatim "exploration only"**; **`data/` contains a `data/README.md` (source & limitations)**; **and `models/` holds the artifact plus `metrics.json` and `feature_spec.json`**. **⑥ ⭐⭐ The contested details point at files a reader can open**: **the full writeup and the actual numbers point to `EXCLUDED_FEATURES` in `fraud_risk/features.py` and to `notebooks/01_eda.ipynb`**. **⑦ ⭐ Readable with the site’s fraud and explainability entries**: [[explainable-ai-fraud]], [[ifraudsimulator]], [[networkfraud]], [[insurance-conformal-fraud]], [[fraud-detection]], [[claims-fraud-guardian]], [[aida-tix-anomaly-detection]], [[claim-fraud-dataset-generator]], [[aws-gnn-fraud-detection]] and [[shap-relativities]].

**③ ⭐⭐⭐ Whether those two guard tests actually exist and pass was not verified** — **pytest was not run and `tests/` was not read**; **this is the single most important thing to verify next for this entry**; **④ ⭐⭐⭐ The figures `chess` 82.6% / `cross-fit` 74.3% / 24.7% base rate were not verified**, **nor was the claim that the API and dashboard emit a warning when that feature appears among top contributors** — **its service was not called**; **⑤ ⭐⭐ Which of its 44 dbt tests "caught a real anomaly in the source data" was not verified**; **⑥ ⭐⭐ Its root-cause judgement (that fraud probability was baked into vehicle and city groupings by the generator) was not verified** — **it rests on the author’s observation of a third-party synthetic dataset**; **the entry does not claim it generalises to other datasets, nor that the original dataset’s authors have confirmed it**; **⑦ ⭐ Whether the same dbt project really runs against both DuckDB and Snowflake was not verified** (**nothing was run**); **⑧ ⭐ ⚠️ The chosen dataset is a synthetic 1,000-row sample, and the author himself states that fields such as `insured_hobbies` do not match real-world mechanisms**; **the entry therefore does not claim its model, metrics or conclusions generalise to any real claims portfolio**; **⑨ ⭐ ⚠️ Fraud scoring is used to make adverse judgements about individuals**, **which engages procedural and compliance requirements in most jurisdictions**; **the entry does not claim the system is usable for any real claim investigation, denial or adverse action**; **⑩ ⭐ The README does not discuss fairness or protected-class impact** (**contrasting with this round’s [[guidewire-claim-intelligence]], which explicitly lists fairness auditing as a first-class evaluation criterion to add**) — **the entry records the difference without judging it**;
